title: Place opposing words on a shared visual fulcrum

motion.summary: A diagonal beam and triangular support form beneath DAY and NIGHT. The words occupy opposite sides and then visibly different heights, turning their contrast into one readable spatial relationship.
phases: DIVIDE establishes the upper-left lead-in with open space below.
DAY appears above the developing beam and central support; FROM remains a small connector.
NIGHT arrives on the opposite side, and DAY rises as NIGHT takes a lower position across the shared fulcrum.
motion.transferablePrinciple: Express contrast through the relative position of two intact words around a shared geometric relationship, rather than through isolated title changes.
variations: In a choice scene, let two readable alternatives settle at different distances from an invented central decision point.
For reconciliation, establish opposed heights first, then create a new shared level when the meaning changes.
cautions: Use a fulcrum only when comparison or opposition fits the scene; an arbitrary seesaw becomes decoration.
A beam does not prove physically coherent weight or motion; this source is an expressive diagram.
Keep the connector phrase readable and allow both terms to be present before their relative position changes.
